complexity.correctness_reason: A skewed tree deeper than CPython's recursion limit (~1000 frames) raises RecursionError, which the 100-node cap prevents but the generalized problem allows.
complexity.notes: Space is O(h) for the recursion stack: O(log n) on the balanced trees the benchmark generates, but O(n) on a skewed tree. Converting to an explicit-stack or level-order iteration would remove the recursion-depth failure mode at the cost of the same O(n) auxiliary space. The else after a return is unneeded but harmless.
complexity.summary: Plain recursive DFS: the depth of a node is 1 plus the max of its children's depths, with an empty tree returning 0. Every node is visited exactly once.
